newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica leaves door open for Cuban asylum-seekers.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica leaves door open for Cuban asylum-seekers.

text.p: Jamaica has abandoned talks with Cuba over the return of asylum-seekers, Foreign Minister Seymour Mullings said on Saturday.
"There is nothing we can do to stop Cubans from making an attempt to enter Jamaica," Mullings told reporters.
Cuba's communist government said last May it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Jamaica on the return of Cubans who had fled to Jamaica to seek asylym.

The agreement was criticised in Jamaica and abroad and Mullings responded then by saying it was not binding as cabinet had yet to ratify it. He said on Saturday no further talks were planned to pursue the matter.
"I think the Cubans understand Jamaica's position on this matter," Mullings said, declining to elaborate further.

When the Cuban refugee crisis reached a peak last April, government officials said they feared accepting the 60 asylum-seekers then in Jamaica would cause a flood that would swamp its meagre resources.
The government ruled that all 60 were economic and not political refugees and decided to return them to Cuba. But over half managed to flee to the Dominican Republic where they were given residence.
Mullings said if any more Cubans made it to Jamaica, "We will have them processed in a manner as defined by international conventions and regulations."
